summary.oneLiner: with cost-to-income already inching down. The story is now three converging optionalities, HNI + ET Money reaching break-even this year, the B&K institutional-equities/ECM integration turning broking more annuity-like, and the UBS collaboration beginning to move money both ways, half mix), but management insists per-line margins are intact.

one-line thesis: A clean compounding quarter for India's premium UHNI/alternates franchise: total ARR AUM +19% to Rs 3.42 lakh cr (wealth +24.2%, AMC +8.2%), ARR revenue +20.3% and PAT +14.8% to Rs 330 cr, with cost-to-income already inching down (53.5% → 51.3%). The story is now three converging optionalities — HNI + ET Money reaching break-even this year, the B&K institutional-equities/ECM integration turning broking more annuity-like, and the UBS collaboration beginning to move money both ways — all layered on a structurally under-penetrated wealth market. Near-term optics: AMC net flows were negative on a single institutional redemption ($550-600M → $175-180M) and headline ARR retention slipped ~4 bps (half carry, half mix), but management insists per-line margins are intact.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total ARR AUM | Rs 3,42,000 cr | +19% | Wealth ARR AUM Rs 2,42,000 cr (+24.2%); AMC AUM Rs 1,00,000 cr (+8.2%, crossed Rs 1 lakh cr) |
| Overall AUM | Rs 7.8 lakh cr | +17% | As on 30-Jun-2026 |
| ARR net flows | Rs 10,815 cr | — | vs Rs 8,985 cr prev quarter; Wealth flows Rs 13,379 cr (vs Rs 6,957 cr Q4); AMC net **negative** on one institutional redemption |
| ARR revenue | Rs 614 cr | +20.3% | 75% of total revenue from operations |
| ARR retention | 74 bps | vs ~78 bps | Wealth 71 bps, AMC 83 bps; ~2-2.5 bps of the drop = carry, rest = mix |
| TBR (transaction/brokerage) | Rs 208 cr | +37.3% | Core Rs 125-150 cr run-rate + carry (~4 bps of ~Rs 60,000 cr AIF AUM) |
| Total revenue | Rs 870 cr | +20% | |
| Total cost / C-I ratio | Rs 446 cr / **51.3%** | vs 53.5% Q4FY26 | Incl. ~Rs 12-13 cr exceptional ESOP cost (B&K acquisition) |
| PAT | **Rs 330 cr** | **+14.8%** | |
| Tangible ROE | 19.4% | — | Expected to improve as lending/AMC capital earns |
> Adjustments: Rs 12-13 cr exceptional ESOP cost tied to the B&K deal sits in this quarter's cost base. AMC "negative net flows" is one large partial redemption ($550-600M → $175-180M), not broad-based — gross AMC flows were still ~Rs 4,000 cr.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Net flows:** ~12-15% of opening ARR AUM (~Rs 35-40,000 cr for FY27), split ~70:30 to 75:25 in favour of wealth.
- **Cost-to-income:** improve ~100-150 bps for full-year FY27; Q4 exit ~49-49.5% (desire is ~49-50% full-year exit).
- **HNI business:** break-even and "a little bit of profitability this year itself"; **ET Money** break-even by Q4FY27 (run-rate loss now ~Rs 3-4 cr/qtr ex-exit costs, ~Rs 6-7 cr this quarter).
- **UBS collaboration:** conservative ~$500-600M AUM to be exchanged both ways over ~a year (started Jan-Mar'26); funds launching both ways in the coming quarter.
- **RM count:** toward 350-400 senior RMs (adding ~30-40/yr over 3 yrs); **UHNI families 9-10,000 in 3 years** (from 4,100).
- **TBR / broking:** transaction+brokerage toward Rs 750-1,000 cr over 2-3 yrs (ECM ~15-20% of that); listed equity brokerage ~Rs 75 cr/qtr (Rs 310-320 cr annualized run-rate), growing 15-20%/yr; TBR to stay ~20-25% of revenue (rising in quality, not lumpiness).
- **Carry:** ~3-5 bps of AIF alternates AUM (~Rs 240 cr/yr on ~Rs 60,000 cr).
- **SARs:** newly announced ~12 lakh SARs → ~Rs 60 cr cost spread over 4 years, starting next quarter (once allotted).
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business — pipeline = flow momentum + product launches. ARR net flows Rs 10,815 cr (wealth Rs 13,379 cr the driver); "a lot of product launches planned for the next 6-9 months" to balance wealth vs AMC flows. Alternates AUM ~Rs 58-60,000 cr; AMC AUM crossed Rs 1 lakh cr. Clients with >Rs 10 cr grew from ~1,800-2,000 (36 months ago) to >4,000. ECM/IB team building (4 coverage + process/compliance hires) — full-strength by Oct-Dec 2026, pitching actively from ~Jan 2027.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Wealth (UHNI):** anchor franchise; addressable 40,000-45,000 households; three vectors — wallet-share deepening, beyond top cities, first-choice post-monetization. Advisory ~30-35 bps, discretionary 40-45 bps, distribution 65-70 bps.
- **HNI:** ~60+ RMs across 12 locations, >Rs 5,000 cr AUM (from ~Rs 600 cr → Rs 4,000 cr last yr → Rs 5,100-5,200 cr now), 800+ clients at ~90 bps; digital-first feeder into UHNI (200,000+ household TAM); revenue recognized with a 12-month lag (~Rs 7-8 cr trail started).
- **Asset Management / alternates:** PE, private credit, real estate, infra, renewables, multi-asset + listed; AUM >Rs 1 lakh cr; broadening AIF/PMS/MF/SIF shelf. PMS structurally migrating into AIF/MF/SIF pooled structures.
- **Institutional equities (B&K):** 550+ mid/small-cap companies covered, 300+ institutional clients, >85% of broking from cash segment; access to 600+ corporate treasuries feeding cross-sell; combined listed-equity brokerage ~Rs 310-320 cr run-rate (was Rs 250-260 cr at deal close).
- **ET Money:** FY26 reset toward profitability; break-even targeted this year.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) **UBS global collaboration** — offshore distribution for alternates/listed + NRI/resident/global cross-referrals. 2) **HNI feeder** into UHNI at scale. 3) **B&K ECM/IB** build-out (mandates from ~Jan 2027). 4) **Private credit** — management sees it growing as fast as PE over time (they operate the 10-11% and 13-15% buckets, "negligible to zero accidents" over 7-8 yrs). 5) **Migration of ~4,000 sub-scale (Rs 1-10 cr) clients** into the HNI servicing model over the next 3 months.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Advisory practice at scale is the moat** — "at scale to build an advisory practice with this retention has not been that easy… building a product model is easier, scaling it is tougher; on advisory the service model is tougher to build and even tougher to charge fees." Advisory clients cross-use the platform ~3x a distribution client (trust, GIFT City, lending, brokerage), so blended retention is "not dramatically different" despite lower headline advisory bps.
- **"Two-and-a-half advisor" positioning** — clients typically end with 2-2.5 advisors (from 4-5 at start); 360 ONE's ability to be in the core two is the durable relationship advantage.
- **Private-credit track record** — negligible-to-zero credit accidents over 7-8 years in the 10-15% buckets; regulator-enforced no-gated-redemption structure keeps the industry clean.
margins & cost dynamics: Headline ARR retention 78 → ~73-74 bps: ~2-2.5 bps is carry recognition (mostly AMC), ~1-2 bps is business mix (advisory lower-yield than distribution; TBR seasonally softer in Q1-Q2). Per-line margins unchanged. The only structural retention drag is the pure listed-AMC book (~8-9% of revenue). Cost-to-income bridge from 50-51% → ~47%: driven by HNI + ET Money break-even + operating leverage — **not** by cutting UHNI hiring (stable UHNI C-I ~45%, +100-200 bps for perpetual expansion/ramp).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light. Investment is in RM capacity, technology, portfolio analytics, client-data security, and team acquisition. GB/JB (guaranteed/joining bonus) dynamics stretch the hiring-to-productivity cycle to ~24-30 months (from 12-18), a modest ongoing cost-to-income drag.
capital allocation: Deploying capital into lending and asset-management businesses (expected to lift ROE from 19.4%). B&K acquisition integration (ESOP/exceptional costs flowing through). SARs of ~Rs 60 cr over 4 years as retention comp. No dividend specifics on call.
risks & watch-items: 1) **AMC lumpiness** — single institutional redemptions can turn net flows negative (as this quarter); global allocations to listed India equity muted 6-9 months. 2) **Retention drift** on the listed-AMC book (structural). 3) **Execution on cost-to-income** — must actually land the 100-150 bps FY27 improvement while hiring 30-40 RMs/yr. 4) **UBS collaboration** still early — unit economics deliberately undisclosed. 5) **Key-man / succession** — Bain step-back chatter around Karan Bhagat's tenure (he pushed back firmly). 6) **Carry volatility** quarter-to-quarter.
management quality / tone: Karan Bhagat highly confident, granular and candid — walked through cost-to-income bridges, retention decomposition, flow colour and the "two-and-a-half advisor" framing without dodging. Addressed the succession question head-on ("answered it 125 times… all of 49… 90%+ invested financially"). Transparent that AMC flows were lopsided on one redemption and that PMS is structurally migrating. Slightly reluctant on UBS unit economics ("wait and see over six months"). Overall: credible, execution-focused, owner-operator tone.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The profit engine is shifting from AUM growth to cost-to-income + break-evens** — HNI and ET Money flipping to break-even, plus operating leverage, is what bridges 51% → 47% C-I, independent of market beta.
- **B&K is quietly becoming an annuity + cross-sell asset**, not just broking — 600+ corporate treasury relationships feed wealth/treasury/lending, and listed-equity brokerage (~Rs 75 cr/qtr) is being reframed as a low-lumpiness, 15-20%-growth line rather than a cyclical trade.
- **PMS is structurally shrinking into AIF/MF/SIF** — same clients, same strategies, better pooled vehicles; a mix headwind to reported PMS but not to economics.
- **Client-count, not AUM, is the "acid test"** management watches — >Rs 10 cr clients 2,000 → 4,000+ over 3 years, targeting 8-10,000, because wallet-share expansion compounds on top.

business_model.body:
- Self-described as "one of India's largest wealth and alternates asset managers", and 360 ONE Asset as "Pioneer & Leader in Alternate Asset Management in India"; the cover frames three pillars: "Uniquely Positioned", "Full Stack Platform" and "Shareholder Value".
- Wealth Management targets UHNIs with "a focus on clients with INR 50+ Crs financial net worth", caters to "4,000+ families with an AUM of over INR 4,50,000 Crs", and runs "a deep platform to service 600+ corporate treasuries".
- Alternates franchise claims the "largest bouquet of pre-IPO, mid-stage and early-stage funds in the industry", "market leader in the fast-growing Private Credit segment" and "amongst largest investors in organized REITs / InvITs".
- "Exclusive strategic collaboration with UBS - a global endorsement of the franchise", covering bi-directional client referrals, cross-platform product access and best-practice exchange in Wealth.
- Awards cited: "200+ AWARDS IN 18 YEARS", including India's Best Wealth Manager at Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026, Best Private Bank - India at Asian Private Banker's 15th Awards for Distinction, Best Private Equity House at Global Private Banking Innovation Awards 2026, and Best Private Credit Deal (360 ONE Asset) at FinanceAsia Achievement Awards 2025.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Wealth (UHNI):** anchor franchise; addressable 40,000-45,000 households; three vectors — wallet-share deepening, beyond top cities, first-choice post-monetization. Advisory ~30-35 bps, discretionary 40-45 bps, distribution 65-70 bps.
- **HNI:** ~60+ RMs across 12 locations, >Rs 5,000 cr AUM (from ~Rs 600 cr → Rs 4,000 cr last yr → Rs 5,100-5,200 cr now), 800+ clients at ~90 bps; digital-first feeder into UHNI (200,000+ household TAM); revenue recognized with a 12-month lag (~Rs 7-8 cr trail started).
- **Asset Management / alternates:** PE, private credit, real estate, infra, renewables, multi-asset + listed; AUM >Rs 1 lakh cr; broadening AIF/PMS/MF/SIF shelf. PMS structurally migrating into AIF/MF/SIF pooled structures.
- **Institutional equities (B&K):** 550+ mid/small-cap companies covered, 300+ institutional clients, >85% of broking from cash segment; access to 600+ corporate treasuries feeding cross-sell; combined listed-equity brokerage ~Rs 310-320 cr run-rate (was Rs 250-260 cr at deal close).
- **ET Money:** FY26 reset toward profitability; break-even targeted this year.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not an order-book business — pipeline = flow momentum + product launches. ARR net flows Rs 10,815 cr (wealth Rs 13,379 cr the driver); "a lot of product launches planned for the next 6-9 months" to balance wealth vs AMC flows. Alternates AUM ~Rs 58-60,000 cr; AMC AUM crossed Rs 1 lakh cr. Clients with >Rs 10 cr grew from ~1,800-2,000 (36 months ago) to >4,000. ECM/IB team building (4 coverage + process/compliance hires) — full-strength by Oct-Dec 2026, pitching actively from ~Jan 2027.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Net flows:** ~12-15% of opening ARR AUM (~Rs 35-40,000 cr for FY27), split ~70:30 to 75:25 in favour of wealth.
- **Cost-to-income:** improve ~100-150 bps for full-year FY27; Q4 exit ~49-49.5% (desire is ~49-50% full-year exit).
- **HNI business:** break-even and "a little bit of profitability this year itself"; **ET Money** break-even by Q4FY27 (run-rate loss now ~Rs 3-4 cr/qtr ex-exit costs, ~Rs 6-7 cr this quarter).
- **UBS collaboration:** conservative ~$500-600M AUM to be exchanged both ways over ~a year (started Jan-Mar'26); funds launching both ways in the coming quarter.
- **RM count:** toward 350-400 senior RMs (adding ~30-40/yr over 3 yrs); **UHNI families 9-10,000 in 3 years** (from 4,100).
- **TBR / broking:** transaction+brokerage toward Rs 750-1,000 cr over 2-3 yrs (ECM ~15-20% of that); listed equity brokerage ~Rs 75 cr/qtr (Rs 310-320 cr annualized run-rate), growing 15-20%/yr; TBR to stay ~20-25% of revenue (rising in quality, not lumpiness).
- **Carry:** ~3-5 bps of AIF alternates AUM (~Rs 240 cr/yr on ~Rs 60,000 cr).
- **SARs:** newly announced ~12 lakh SARs → ~Rs 60 cr cost spread over 4 years, starting next quarter (once allotted).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 1) **UBS global collaboration** — offshore distribution for alternates/listed + NRI/resident/global cross-referrals. 2) **HNI feeder** into UHNI at scale. 3) **B&K ECM/IB** build-out (mandates from ~Jan 2027). 4) **Private credit** — management sees it growing as fast as PE over time (they operate the 10-11% and 13-15% buckets, "negligible to zero accidents" over 7-8 yrs). 5) **Migration of ~4,000 sub-scale (Rs 1-10 cr) clients** into the HNI servicing model over the next 3 months.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Headline ARR retention 78 → ~73-74 bps: ~2-2.5 bps is carry recognition (mostly AMC), ~1-2 bps is business mix (advisory lower-yield than distribution; TBR seasonally softer in Q1-Q2). Per-line margins unchanged. The only structural retention drag is the pure listed-AMC book (~8-9% of revenue). Cost-to-income bridge from 50-51% → ~47%: driven by HNI + ET Money break-even + operating leverage — **not** by cutting UHNI hiring (stable UHNI C-I ~45%, +100-200 bps for perpetual expansion/ramp).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Deploying capital into lending and asset-management businesses (expected to lift ROE from 19.4%). B&K acquisition integration (ESOP/exceptional costs flowing through). SARs of ~Rs 60 cr over 4 years as retention comp. No dividend specifics on call.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Karan Bhagat highly confident, granular and candid — walked through cost-to-income bridges, retention decomposition, flow colour and the "two-and-a-half advisor" framing without dodging. Addressed the succession question head-on ("answered it 125 times… all of 49… 90%+ invested financially"). Transparent that AMC flows were lopsided on one redemption and that PMS is structurally migrating. Slightly reluctant on UBS unit economics ("wait and see over six months"). Overall: credible, execution-focused, owner-operator tone.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL)
moat.body:
- **Advisory practice at scale is the moat** — "at scale to build an advisory practice with this retention has not been that easy… building a product model is easier, scaling it is tougher; on advisory the service model is tougher to build and even tougher to charge fees." Advisory clients cross-use the platform ~3x a distribution client (trust, GIFT City, lending, brokerage), so blended retention is "not dramatically different" despite lower headline advisory bps.
- **"Two-and-a-half advisor" positioning** — clients typically end with 2-2.5 advisors (from 4-5 at start); 360 ONE's ability to be in the core two is the durable relationship advantage.
- **Private-credit track record** — negligible-to-zero credit accidents over 7-8 years in the 10-15% buckets; regulator-enforced no-gated-redemption structure keeps the industry clean.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) **AMC lumpiness** — single institutional redemptions can turn net flows negative (as this quarter); global allocations to listed India equity muted 6-9 months. 2) **Retention drift** on the listed-AMC book (structural). 3) **Execution on cost-to-income** — must actually land the 100-150 bps FY27 improvement while hiring 30-40 RMs/yr. 4) **UBS collaboration** still early — unit economics deliberately undisclosed. 5) **Key-man / succession** — Bain step-back chatter around Karan Bhagat's tenure (he pushed back firmly). 6) **Carry volatility** quarter-to-quarter.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The profit engine is shifting from AUM growth to cost-to-income + break-evens** — HNI and ET Money flipping to break-even, plus operating leverage, is what bridges 51% → 47% C-I, independent of market beta.
- **B&K is quietly becoming an annuity + cross-sell asset**, not just broking — 600+ corporate treasury relationships feed wealth/treasury/lending, and listed-equity brokerage (~Rs 75 cr/qtr) is being reframed as a low-lumpiness, 15-20%-growth line rather than a cyclical trade.
- **PMS is structurally shrinking into AIF/MF/SIF** — same clients, same strategies, better pooled vehicles; a mix headwind to reported PMS but not to economics.
- **Client-count, not AUM, is the "acid test"** management watches — >Rs 10 cr clients 2,000 → 4,000+ over 3 years, targeting 8-10,000, because wallet-share expansion compounds on top.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Total ARR AUM Rs 3.42 lakh cr (+19%; wealth +24.2%, AMC +8.2%, AMC crossed Rs 1 lakh cr). ARR net flows Rs 10,815 cr (wealth Rs 13,379 cr; AMC net negative on one redemption). ARR revenue Rs 614 cr (+20.3%), TBR Rs 208 cr (+37.3%), total revenue Rs 870 cr (+20%). C-I 51.3% (from 53.5%), PAT Rs 330 cr (+14.8%), tangible ROE 19.4%. Retention 74 bps (down ~4 bps: half carry, half mix). Rs 12-13 cr exceptional ESOP (B&K). Guidance set: FY27 net flows ~12-15% of opening ARR (~Rs 35-40k cr, 70:30-75:25 wealth); C-I -100-150 bps (Q4 exit ~49-49.5%); HNI + ET Money break-even this year; UBS ~$500-600M AUM exchange in ~1 yr; RMs → 350-400 / families → 9-10,000 (3 yrs); TBR → Rs 750-1,000 cr (2-3 yrs); SARs ~Rs 60 cr / 4 yrs.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did AMC net flows recover (product launches)? (2) C-I trajectory toward ~49-50% full-year; (3) HNI break-even + ET Money loss narrowing to break-even by Q4; (4) UBS funds actually launched both ways + first AUM exchanged; (5) B&K brokerage run-rate +15-20%; (6) ECM team full-strength (Oct-Dec) & first mandates; (7) retention holding 70-75 bps._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Partnership] Exclusive strategic collaboration with UBS is presented as a structural franchise asset (bi-directional client referrals, cross-platform product access, best-practice exchange in Wealth), not as a transaction with disclosed terms.
- [Macro thesis] "India is witnessing wealth creation at a pace and breadth never seen before through liquidity events, private equity exits, new-economy listings, and the steady financialisation of savings"; on alternates, "Just as domestic capital transformed public equity over the last decade, it is now scaling into alternatives with real momentum".
- [Disclosure practice] Historical quarter-wise data is "now continued to be reported in a Data Book, maintained in an excel format on our website", covering consolidated data, both segmentals, business summary, capital allocation and annual/quarterly annexures.
- [Exceptional costs] The Wealth Management segment table carries the footnote "* OPBT excludes acquisition related exceptional employment costs", implying acquisition-related exceptional employment costs exist; the deck does not quantify them separately.
- [Flow divergence] Asset Management ARR Net Flows were -2,564 in Q1 FY27 against +2,028 in Q4 FY26 and +973 in Q1 FY26, while Wealth Management ARR Net Flows were 13,379 in Q1 FY27; the deck offers no explanation for the Asset Management outflow.
